equity.level_reason: The comparison is caregivers vs noncaregivers, not an SPD; sex, race and ethnicity, education, employment and income appear only as caregiver composition (Table 1), and age is an adjustment covariate.

level_alternative.reason: If caregiving is read as a social position (an unpaid role with economic burden), outcomes that are themselves determinants (no health coverage, cost barriers to care) are quantified across groups, which meets level 3 without the word disparity.

notes: Medicaid expansion and the COVID-19 pandemic are offered as explanations of overall trends, not of a group difference. Table 1 compares composition (caregiving status as the dependent variable), so it is not a groupwise outcome by SPD.
view_issues: Table 2 marks some unadjusted changes significant by t-test (e.g., COPD, arthritis, diabetes among caregivers) while their age-adjusted p-values are ≥0.05; the text counts only the age-adjusted changes.
